notes.text: The opening introduces the tree Gamma=(S,A,R), with S as vertices, A as edges, and R as the incidence relation. It writes the maps A to P_2(S) and S to P(A), then asserts injectivity for the latter with the two-vertex one-edge graph as exception. That graph is transcribed with two filled vertices and one unheaded segment. This is an account of the manuscript claim, without a proof check.

The author introduces the families (U_s) and (E_a) and defines X by their displayed coproducts. The paragraph beginning Pour tout names the components of the tree “coupé en a_0” and writes the binary decomposition X=X′ union X″, its two displayed parts, and their intersection E_{a_0}.

The lower paragraph calls the decomposition “propre”, gives two inequalities and then a criterion expressed through the terminal vertices and U_s nonempty. Both equivalence abbreviations are visibly sss. The parenthesized condition label remains star|A. These are source statements; their truth was not independently checked in this transcription run.

The mathematical cues leading back to the ink were the following application/injectivity words at the decorated second arrow, the E_a summand beside the open c-shaped coproduct index, and neighbouring a_0 forms beside the b-shaped nested index. The final arrow retains three candidates; c|a and b|0 retain the ink-led first readings. No index has been repaired from the expected parallel formulas.

H supplies an editorial note asking about a_0 membership in A′ and A″. The manuscript interval contains no corresponding words. The note is identified as H’s editorial addition in the apparatus and supplies no authorial doubt annotation.

Five overwritten or cancelled elements are retained: the t revised in Soit, the E candidate beneath Gamma′, the short c|con trace at considérons, the E candidate beneath the last coproduct, and the cancelled E before the inequalities. At Soit the shared Soi remains live and is written once.

This is a handwritten working sheet with no visible title, date, authorial question mark, or instruction to verify a step. The light pencil 27 at lower left is recorded as an archive sheet-number comment. The reading uncertainties are editorial and are marked in place.
